subject: كون_1:#2
detail: Standalone يَكُونُ does not express a plain present 'is' in MSA; it reads as habitual/future ('patience will be / tends to be beautiful'). Use a context that needs يكون (e.g. after أن/لن, or a habitual frame) or translate accordingly; the Bosnian gloss 'bude' also conflicts with the sentence 'je'.

subject: خلق_1:#4
detail: Using خَلَقْتُ for a person shaping clay is theologically delicate (the Quran reserves this usage for Isa by God's permission) and should be avoided for a learner; the Bosnian 'Oblikovao sam oblik' is a clumsy tautology and the English 'figure' differs from the gloss 'shape'. Replace with a sentence where the agent is God or a negated human claim.

subject: كفر_1:#1
detail: The Bosnian 'Vjernik ne poriče' is unnatural without an object and does not convey kufr; render e.g. 'Vjernik ne niječe (vjeru)' / 'Vjernik ne postaje nevjernik', and align the gloss.

subject: كذب_2:#0
detail: كَذَّبَ الرَّسُولَ means called the messenger a liar; Bosnian 'je poricao poslanika' is unnatural (and imperfective for a single act). Use e.g. 'Nevjernik je poslanika u laž utjerao' / 'proglasio lažljivcem'.

subject: أخذ_8:#0
detail: اتَّخَذَ with a single object means 'took/made for oneself'; 'The man took a friend' / 'Čovjek je uzeo prijatelja' is unnatural and misleading. Translate as 'The man made (took) a friend for himself' / 'Čovjek je stekao prijatelja', or use the two-object pattern.

subject: أخذ_8:#3
detail: 'They took a house' / 'Uzeli su kuću' does not convey اتَّخَذُوا بَيْتًا ('they made/took for themselves a house'); translate as 'They made themselves a house' / 'Napravili su sebi kuću' or use the two-object pattern.

subject: أخذ_8:#4
detail: 'She took a friend' / 'Uzela je prijateljicu' is unnatural for اتَّخَذَتْ صَدِيقَةً; translate as 'She made a friend (for herself)' / 'Stekla je prijateljicu', or use the two-object pattern.

subject: خلق_1:past:ana
detail: خَلَقْتُ (I created) is God's own speech in the Quran; a practice sentence would put invented words in God's mouth, and for a person it is theologically delicate. Decide whether this cell gets a sentence at all.

subject: أخذ_8:#5
detail: English "The man made himself a friend" is unidiomatic and can read as "built a friend"; use "The man took a friend" or "The man made a friend" (matching the Bosnian "stekao je prijatelja").

subject: خلق_1:past:ana
detail: خَلَقْتُ (I created) is God's own speech in the Quran; a practice sentence would put invented words in God's mouth, and for a person it is theologically delicate. Decide whether this cell gets a sentence at all.

subject: أخذ_8:#8
detail: اتَّخَذَ الرَّجُلُ صَدِيقًا is correct, fully vowelled MSA: Form VIII past 3ms with a single object, as in Quranic اتَّخَذَ خَلِيلًا. 'Made a friend' / 'stekao je prijatelja' is a natural rendering, though it loses a little of the sense of deliberately choosing someone as a friend. The English gloss 'took (for himself), adopted' and the Bosnian gloss 'stekao je' are both acceptable. Nothing theologically sensitive.

subject: وحي_4:past:ana
detail: أَوْحَيْتُ (I revealed) is said only by God in the Quran; a practice sentence would put first-person revelation in a speaker's mouth. The MSA sense "I suggested" is possible but misleading for this verb.

subject: وحي_4:past:nahnu
detail: أَوْحَيْنَا (We revealed) is said only by God in the Quran; a practice sentence would invent divine speech. The MSA sense "we suggested" is possible but misleading for this verb.

subject: سأل_1:imperative:anta
detail: The engine table has only the Uthmani spelling سْـَٔلِ (from وَسْـَٔلِ, 12:82) and no generated MSA form, and CAMeL does not read اسْأَلْ or سَلْ as an imperative, so no standard spelling can pass the cell check. Needs a generated/alternative form (اسْأَلْ, سَلْ) in the table.

subject: فعل_1:#0
detail: Bosnian "Čovjek je uradio dobro" reads as "the man did (it) well"; use "Čovjek je učinio dobro (djelo)" / "Čovjek je činio dobro".

subject: أمر_1:#0
detail: أَمَرَ الْمَلِكُ الْجُنُودَ means "gave the soldiers an order"; Bosnian "Kralj je naredio vojnicima" is left hanging (ordered what?). Use "Kralj je izdao naredbu vojnicima" / EN "The king gave the soldiers an order", or add the content of the order (e.g. بِالْهُجُومِ).

subject: أمر_1:#3
detail: Translations weaken the target verb: "told"/"rekli smo" should be "ordered"/"naredili smo" ("We ordered the child to pray." / "Naredili smo djetetu da klanja."), matching the gloss.

subject: أمر_1:#4
detail: الصِّدْقِ is truthfulness, not sincerity: gloss "with sincerity"/"iskrenost" is wrong (use "truthfulness"/"iskrenost u govoru" or "istinoljubivost"). English "They command truthfulness" is unnatural; use "They enjoin truthfulness." / Bosnian "Naređuju istinoljubivost" (or "Traže da se govori istina").

subject: جزي_1:#1
detail: تَجْزِي الْأُمُّ ابْنَهَا is unnatural MSA: جَزَى needs what is repaid (e.g. خَيْرًا or بِـ...), and "reward a son" is normally كَافَأَ. Rephrase, e.g. تَجْزِي الْأُمُّ ابْنَهَا خَيْرًا عَلَى صَبْرِهِ, with matching translations.
